The IRGC announced that it had targeted two Patriot air defense radars at the Riffa and Awali bases in Bahrain with missiles and drones. It added that Aerospace Force fighters had struck US military positions at both bases shortly before the statement was issued. The IRGC said the strikes came in response to continued aggression against Iran and the violation of its airspace by two drones, identified as MQ-1 and MQ-9 models. It stressed that Iran’s airspace is a red line for the country’s Armed Forces, warning that any violation by another country or aggressor force would be met with a strong and decisive response from Iranian fighters. The statement also said that US military escort and aerial cover operations, which had been underway since dawn, had failed to achieve their objectives. According to the IRGC, US military equipment and naval vessels operating under its protection had sustained heavy losses at sea and in the air.

🗳️ Argentina has become Spain’s largest overseas electoral district: As of this Saturday, 520,203 people are eligible to vote in the elections that will determine whether Pedro Sánchez’s government remains in power or whether a coalition between the People’s Party and Vox takes office. 📍 Of those eligible, 331,000 are voting at the Consulate General in Buenos Aires, and the rest at diplomatic missions in Rosario, Mendoza, Bahía Blanca, and Córdoba. ⚖️ Voting is underway amid controversy over a decision by the Spanish Supreme Court, which invalidated the votes of many individuals naturalized under the “grandchildren law” because they failed to prove they were descendants of political exiles. 📊 In total, 2.75 million Spaniards are registered in the Electoral Roll for Absent Residents; Argentina is home to the largest community.
